description: Establish the green baseline on the perf/fast-browser-loop branch, add the flag-gated config surface (default OFF) and the PURE data shapes the fast browser loop depends on. This is the foundational-thinking step: design the types and the boundary flag BEFORE any behavior, so the rest of the work slots into a stable, compiling core with the current suite untouched. No behavior changes and the default path is byte-identical.
steps: Confirm the branch is perf/fast-browser-loop (base main). Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run build`, `pnpm test`. Record the pass/skip counts as the baseline (expected ~263 passed / 3 skipped).

In src/config.ts: add a new flag `LAYA_FAST_LOOP` parsed ONCE, following the EXACT existing pattern of the boolean env flags (e.g. LAYA_SETTLE_PROBE / LAYA_LOOP_DETECTION). Add `export const DEFAULT_FAST_LOOP = false;`, a `fastLoop: boolean` field on LayaBrowserConfig, a `fastLoop?: boolean` on ConfigOverrides, parse it in loadConfig with default false, and document it in the top-of-file env comment block (NO em dashes). Also add two adaptive-wait bound constants following the existing MIN/MAX pattern: `DEFAULT_FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS = 200`, `FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS_MIN = 0`, `FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS_MAX = 2000`, parsed from `LAYA_FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS` into a `fastWaitCapMs: number` config field (clamped), default 200. This mirrors jev's 200ms autocomplete cap.

In src/config.test.ts: add assertions that loadConfig() defaults fastLoop to false and fastWaitCapMs to 200, that LAYA_FAST_LOOP=true flips it, and that LAYA_FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS clamps out-of-range values, following the existing config test patterns.

In src/types.ts (KEEP PURE - no playwright/onnx imports): add the fast-path data shapes. (a) `export interface NodeGuard` - a pure, JSON-serializable semantic-freshness fingerprint of one node captured at decision time, mirroring jev's guard array but as a NAMED STRUCT so illegal states are unrepresentable: fields { role: string; name: string; value: string | null; checked: boolean | null; selectedIndex: number | null; disabled: boolean; ariaExpanded: string | null; ariaChecked: string | null; ariaSelected: string | null; href: string | null; scopeText: string } (scopeText is the truncated innerText of the nearest form/dialog/row/list-item scope). (b) Extend Control with an OPTIONAL `nodeId?: number` (the persistent in-page identity from the fast snapshot; absent on the legacy domwalk/aria path so existing callers are unaffected). (c) `export interface FastControl extends Control` carrying required `nodeId: number`, a `guard: NodeGuard`, and a `rect: { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number }` (geometry for the pre-input occlusion hit-test). (d) `export interface FastSnapshot` = { url; title; visibleText; controls: FastControl[]; text: string; pageKey: string; marker: string } - the atomic single-call snapshot result. Add thorough doc comments (NO em dashes) explaining each field mirrors the jev mechanic and that FastSnapshot is validated at the browser boundary because it originates from an untrusted page.evaluate.

In src/types.test.ts: add a couple of pure unit tests constructing a NodeGuard / FastControl / FastSnapshot literal to lock the shapes (they compile and round-trip through JSON), matching the existing pure-type test style.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm run typecheck and pnpm run build pass with the new types and config field.
pnpm test passes with the same pass count as baseline plus the new config/type assertions (no regressions, still 3 skipped).
loadConfig() defaults fastLoop=false and fastWaitCapMs=200; LAYA_FAST_LOOP=true and LAYA_FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS are honored/clamped (asserted in config.test.ts).
src/types.ts still imports neither playwright nor @receptron/laya (grep confirms it stays pure).
No em dashes in any new comment or doc string.
verification: Run `pnpm run typecheck` and confirm it exits 0.
Run `pnpm run build` and confirm it exits 0.
Run `pnpm test` and confirm all pass with only the expected 3 skips.
Run `grep -n "playwright\|@receptron" src/types.ts` and confirm no matches (pure module).
findings:
Done on branch perf/fast-browser-loop (base main). BASELINE before changes: pnpm run typecheck exit 0, pnpm run build exit 0, pnpm test = 39 files, 263 passed | 3 skipped (266). The 3 skips are the expected WebKit self-skip + 2 LAYA_MODEL_DIR-gated blocks.

CONFIG (src/config.ts): added flag LAYA_FAST_LOOP parsed once via envBoolDefaultFalse (default false) following the LAYA_LOOP_DETECTION/LAYA_SETTLE_PROBE boolean pattern; added DEFAULT_FAST_LOOP=false and the MIN/MAX clamp trio DEFAULT_FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS=200 / FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS_MIN=0 / FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS_MAX=2000 following the SELF_HEAL_RETRIES pattern; parsed LAYA_FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS via parseNumber+clamp into fastWaitCapMs (default 200). Added fastLoop:boolean and fastWaitCapMs:number to LayaBrowserConfig, fastLoop?/fastWaitCapMs? to ConfigOverrides, wired into the returned config object, and documented both env vars in the top-of-file comment block (no em dashes).

TYPES (src/types.ts, kept PURE): added Control.nodeId?:number (optional, absent on legacy path). Added named structs NodeGuard, FastControl (extends Control; requires nodeId, guard:NodeGuard, rect{x,y,w,h}), and FastSnapshot{url,title,visibleText,controls:FastControl[],text,pageKey,marker}. Thorough doc comments explain each field mirrors the jev mechanic and that FastSnapshot is validated at the browser boundary because it comes from an untrusted page.evaluate. No em dashes in any new comment.

TESTS: test/config.test.ts +3 assertions (defaults fastLoop=false/fastWaitCapMs=200; LAYA_FAST_LOOP=true flips; LAYA_FAST_WAIT_CAP_MS clamp/out-of-range). test/types.test.ts +3 pure tests constructing NodeGuard/FastControl/FastSnapshot literals that compile and round-trip through JSON.

VERIFICATION after changes: pnpm run typecheck exit 0; pnpm run build exit 0; targeted vitest test/config.test.ts (28->31) + test/types.test.ts (5->8) all pass; full pnpm test = 39 files, 269 passed | 3 skipped (272) - exactly baseline+6 new, no regressions, still 3 skipped. Purity confirmed: `grep -n "playwright|@receptron" src/types.ts` matches only two pre-existing doc-comment references (lines 4 and 348), and there are zero import statements in the file. Em-dash grep on new content is clean; the only em dashes in src/types.ts and src/config.ts are on pre-existing lines untouched by this feature. Default path is byte-identical (fastLoop defaults false, nodeId optional/absent on legacy path).
